styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Hassan II Mosque, the old medina and the Art Deco centre.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, tagines and cheap street eats.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Old walls, the Habous quarter and colonial streets.

stays.why: Walk to the medina, the old walls and the Art Deco streets. Best base for first-timers without a car.
Quieter business and shopping district with big hotels; short taxi ride to the Corniche and the centre.
Sea views and beach clubs; good for evenings by the water, but you will need taxis for the sights.
Near the new medina, the royal palace gates and the market; calm and traditional, a bit away from nightlife.

food: Try Moroccan classics: tagine, couscous (often on Fridays) and harira soup. A simple sit-down meal is often around 60–120 MAD.
Head to the Central Market (Marché Central) area for fish and seafood; pick your fish and agree the price first.
Cheap eats: msemen pancakes, fresh orange juice and grilled sandwiches in the medina for about 15–40 MAD.
Mint tea and pastries in the Habous quarter make a good mid-afternoon break.
Alcohol is limited outside hotels and licensed restaurants. Check before you plan a drink with dinner.
more_time: Add a coastal day to El Jadida for the Portuguese cistern and old walls; check train times on the day.
Swap one city afternoon for Rabat by train if you want more history and a calmer medina.
Beach lovers can spend a lazy afternoon at a Corniche beach club instead of another museum.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the mosque, the medina and the Habous quarter at an easy pace, with time for a long lunch.

month_notes: January: cool and damp, highs near 18°C and about 6 rain days. Pack a jacket.
February: similar to January, around 18°C with about 7 rain days.
March: mild at about 19°C but the wettest month, around 9 rain days. Keep a rain layer.
April: warming to about 21°C with fewer showers, about 6 rain days. Good walking weather.
May: pleasant and mostly dry, highs near 24°C and about 4 rain days.
June: warm and dry, highs around 25°C with only about 2 rain days.
July: hot and dry, highs near 27°C and no rain expected. Use sunscreen and shade.
August: the hottest month, highs around 28°C, dry. Plan indoor sights at midday.
September: still warm at about 27°C with about 1 rain day. Sea is at its warmest.
October: comfortable at about 25°C, but rain returns with about 5 rain days.
November: cooler at about 21°C with around 6 rain days. Bring a light jacket.
December: cool and showery, highs near 19°C and about 6 rain days.

climate_guide.summary: Mild coastal climate: warm dry summers and cool, sometimes wet winters. Rain is light but most likely from November to March.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Warm and almost rain-free, highs of 24–28°C. Ideal for the Corniche and long walks.

items.title: Wettest months: November to March
items.text: About 6–9 rain days a month. Showers are usually short; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Mild winters
items.text: January and February sit around 18°C by day and 9–10°C at night. A jacket helps in the evening.

items.title: Sea breeze
items.text: The Atlantic keeps the city cooler than inland Morocco, but evenings by the Corniche can feel chilly.

items.title: Strong summer sun
items.text: July and August are dry and bright. Use sunscreen and avoid midday sun on the beach.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers for summer, a warm layer and rain jacket for winter, plus modest clothing for the mosque.

transit.best: Tram for main streets, red petits taxis or ride apps for everything else.

modes.text: No metro. The tram is the main rail option in the city.
Runs 05:30–22:30. One ride is about 6–8 MAD with a rechargeable card. Good for the centre.
Al Bidaoui train links the airport and some city stops, but stops are far apart. Check times on the day.
Cheap at about 5 MAD, but routes are unclear and pickpockets are a risk. Keep bags close.
Red petits taxis use meters, minimum 7 MAD, and drivers may pick up others. White grand taxis run fixed routes and leave when full. Careem and inDrive work.
Not needed for the centre. Traffic and parking are a hassle; use taxis instead.
Fine in the centre and the medina. Wear comfortable shoes for uneven streets.
